text:
Cheng Li: FYI I pushed the quant bakeoff spreadsheet and a prototype packaging scheme for Optimize profiles. TL;DR: AWQ and GPTQ both hit ~1.8x token/s over FP16 on our 3B testbed but accuracy deltas differ across tasks.
Maria Gomez: link? :eyes:
Cheng Li: https://redwood-internal/sheets/quant-bakeoff-2026 — see the 'summary' tab. I pasted the short conclusions below.
Simon Park: awesome. which models and metrics did we run? p50 latency, accuracy top-line?
Cheng Li: ran LLaMA2-7B, Redward-3B (internal), and Mistral-7B. Metrics: exact-match on our eval prompts, R-1/ROUGE for summarization, and p50/p95 latency on g4dn and A100. Also cost estimate per 1M tokens.
Eva Torres: can you paste the headline numbers here? quick scan in slack is easier.
Cheng Li: sure — summary snippet:
```
Model          | Quant   | acc_delta (vs FP16) | p50 latency | cost ratio
LLaMA2-7B      | GPTQ    | -0.8%                | 85ms        | 0.52x
LLaMA2-7B      | AWQ INT8| -1.9%                | 60ms        | 0.40x
Mistral-7B     | AWQ INT8| -3.4%                | 70ms        | 0.44x
Redward-3B     | FP8     | -0.3%                | 48ms        | 0.62x
Redward-3B     | GPTQ    | -1.2%                | 52ms        | 0.50x
```
Cheng Li: Notes: FP8 (our internal quant engine) keeps highest accuracy but hardware support limits deployment targets. AWQ INT8 gives the biggest latency wins but larger acc regressions on open-vocab QA.
Maria Gomez: For Optimize profiles — what fields are we packaging? Need to be pluggable into both hosted and dedicated pipelines.
Cheng Li: proposed minimal profile schema (serialized as JSON in Optimize):
```
{
  "profile_name": "opt/quant/v1/mistral7b-awq-int8",
  "model": "mistral-7b",
  "quant_method": "awq",
  "bits": "8",
  "kernel": "fused_attn_v2",
  "accuracy_delta": "-3.4%",
  "latency_p50_ms": "70",
  "cost_ratio": "0.44",
  "fallback_chain": ["fp16","gptq-int8"],
  "recommended_targets": ["a100","rtx6000"]
}
```
Simon Park: I like that. rename kernel -> inference_kernel? less generic.
Eva Torres: We should version the profile format too. Maybe add `schema_version: v1` and `profile_id` UUID.
Cheng Li: agreed. updated naming convention recommendation:
- profile namespace: "opt/quant/{schema_version}/{model}/{quant}-{bits}-{kernel}-{short-commit}"
- example: `opt/quant/v1/mistral7b-awq-8-fusedv2-c2a4d`
opt-bot: Generated bakeoff artifact: /artifacts/quant-bakeoff/1763459200/report.html (includes model-by-model waterfall plots + prompt-level regression list)
Maria Gomez: For rollout policies: we need an automatic canary that compares FP16 vs selected quant profile on live traffic for 24h and a regression threshold of 1.5% on our main eval set. Passing triggers auto-rollout.
Simon Park: add a safety net: if latency improves but acc_degradation > threshold, route 25% to FP16 and 75% to quant until human review.
Eva Torres: packaging checklist for Optimize UI: human-readable summary, machine fields (schema_version, profile_id, metrics map), and a small sample prompt set used for the profile so we can reproduce quick checks.
Cheng Li: implementation notes:
- store profiles as single JSON + gzipped torchscript artifacts for custom kernels
- include `validate.sh` that runs a quick perf/accuracy smoke test on target infra
- include `compat.txt` listing supported CUDA / driver / kernel versions
Maria Gomez: sounds good. can we also add a `quality_tags` array like ["safe-for-chat","low-regression"] so non-ML teams can filter?
Cheng Li: yes — add `quality_tags` and `confidence_score` (0-1). confidence uses bootstrap over prompts.
Simon Park: one last thing: name collisions — use `profile_id` as canonical and allow display_name to be mutable.
Eva Torres: who's owning the rollout automation work?
Cheng Li: I'll own the profile schema + Optimize integration. @Simon you own the canary runtime changes. @Maria you own UI additions. Eva you own the doc and QA harness.
Maria Gomez: ok I'll add a PR template for profile uploads and require `validate.sh` output.
opt-bot: Reminder: nextquant meeting Tue 09:30 for bakeoff retrospective :calendar:
Cheng Li: thanks everyone — I'll push the schema PR and attach sample profiles to the artifacts folder.
Maria Gomez: thanks! :thumbsup:
Simon Park: great job, good data to start shipping guarded quant.
Eva Torres: LGTM."
